newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins little changed after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins little changed after recent gains.

text.p: MinFin bonds changed little in low activity on Friday as the market slowed down after recent strong gains, dealers said.
"There were no deals at all in the morning, then we edged up a little," said a dealer with a major Russian bank.

Denis Pakhomov, a Natsionalny Rezervny Bank dealer, said some tranches had firmed on investors' hopes that the International Monetary Fund board would disburse overdue tranches of its $10 billion loan to Russia. At the same time there were enough profit-taking sellers not to raise prices, he said.
The IMF board meets on Friday.
"The IMF news will be another push up for the market, after which we shall fall a bit," Pakhomov said.
The major Russian bank dealer forecast a fluctuating market next week.
"The market's potential is exhausted," he said. "We are waiting for more news."
He said the resistance level for tranche 4 was 63.00 and for tranche 5 44.00 offer.
Dealers said they were waiting for the launch of Russia's one billion mark Eurobond, its second Euroissue, and the closing of the London Club rescheduling.
Russia's Finance Ministry said this week the closing would take place at the end of March or start of April.
